prompt:
Prepare an upstream-ready branch of the AWS->objstore storage refactor in patflynn/trillian-tessera (a fork of transparency-dev/tessera). The fork's `main` contains the refactor (new storage/objstore package wrapping gocloud.dev/blob, storage/aws reduced to a deprecated shim, consolidated cmd/conformance/objstore) PLUS a pile of personal-fork CI scaffolding that must NOT go upstream. Your job: produce a clean branch whose diff against upstream is just the refactor + portable CI, and open a PR against the fork's main showing the cleanup.

SETUP
- Branch off the fork's current main: `git fetch origin && git checkout -b chore/upstream-ready-objstore origin/main`.
- Add the upstream remote for verification: `git remote add upstream https://github.com/transparency-dev/tessera.git 2>/dev/null; git fetch upstream`. Upstream default branch is `main`.

STEP 1 — DELETE these fork-only files/dirs entirely (git rm -r):
- .github/workflows/ci_infra_apply.yml
- .github/workflows/ci_infra_teardown.yml
- deployment/modules/gcp/ci_identity/   (whole dir)
- deployment/modules/gcp/ci_mysql/      (whole dir)
- deployment/live/gcp/ci-identity/      (whole dir)
- deployment/live/gcp/ci-mysql/         (whole dir)
- docs/design/gcp-ci-setup.md
These are Terragrunt IaC + WIF identity + a runbook hard-wired to a personal GCP project. None are upstreamable.

STEP 2 — REVERT one fork-specific regression:
- .github/workflows/benchmark-go-pr.yml: the fork added 'external-data-json-path: ./benchmark-data.json' and 'skip-fetch-gh-pages: true' because the fork has no gh-pages branch. Upstream HAS gh-pages, so restore upstream's version: `git checkout upstream/main -- .github/workflows/benchmark-go-pr.yml`.

STEP 3 — GENERICIZE the GCS conformance lane (.github/workflows/gcp_gcs_conformance.yml). It currently couples to the deleted IaC and a hard-coded instance name. Make it run against a maintainer-provisioned GCP setup referenced only through repo vars/secrets:
- REMOVE the 'Terragrunt apply ci-mysql (on demand)' step entirely (the IaC it called is deleted). Also remove the now-unused env vars 'tofu_version' and 'tg_version'.
- Replace every hard-coded Cloud SQL instance name 'tessera-ci-mysql' (in the 'gcloud sql users create/set-password' and 'gcloud sql databases delete' commands) with ${{ vars.GCP_SQL_INSTANCE }}.
- Reword any comments that reference the nightly ci_infra_teardown / the fork (e.g. the concurrency-group comment) to be neutral and not mention deleted workflows.
- At the top of the file add a comment block listing the repo configuration this lane requires so an upstream maintainer can wire it: vars GCP_PROJECT_ID, GCP_REGION, GCP_CI_SA_EMAIL, GCP_WIF_PROVIDER, GCP_SQL_CONNECTION, GCP_SQL_INSTANCE. Keep the per-run bucket/db create+teardown logic as-is (it is self-contained).
Leave .github/workflows/minio_conformance.yml untouched — it is already fully hermetic and upstream-grade. Keep the legit existing-workflow edits already on the branch (aws_integration_test.yml Dockerfile path -> objstore, go_test.yml target -> ./storage/objstore/...).

STEP 4 — SCRUB personal references (only two files contain them in kept content):
- docs/design/cloud-agnostic-storage.md: reframe as a neutral upstream design note. Line 3 currently reads 'Status: Draft (rev 2) · Owner: patflynn · Scope: personal fork experiment (patflynn/trillian-tessera)' — change to something like 'Status: Proposal · Scope: object-storage backend for Tessera' (drop the owner/personal-fork framing). Reword the phrases 'in the fork', 'after the fork proves it', 'Tolerate in the fork' (around lines 222, 227, 265) to neutral upstream language. Do not mention patflynn or the fork anywhere.
- flake.nix line 2: description currently 'Dev tooling for the patflynn/trillian-tessera fork (GCP CI setup)' — change to a neutral description like 'Dev tooling for Tessera (Go toolchain + cloud SDKs)'. Since the GCP CI IaC is removed, also drop the opentofu and terragrunt packages from the flake devShell (and from flake.lock if they appear as inputs) but KEEP google-cloud-sdk, the Go toolchain, and golangci-lint. Run `nix flake check` if nix is available; if not, just ensure the file is syntactically consistent.
- Also grep the whole tree for leftover refs after your edits: `git grep -nIE 'patflynn|tessera-498520|big\.pat|personal fork|the fork'` must return nothing. Fix any stragglers (e.g. deployment/README.md may describe the deleted GCP CI infra — trim those sections; check deployment/live/aws/codelab/README.md too).

STEP 5 — VERIFY before committing:
- `go build ./...` must pass.
- `go vet ./storage/objstore/... ./cmd/conformance/...` must pass.
- Run the object-store unit tests that don't need a live cloud: `go test ./storage/objstore/... -is_mysql_test_optional=true` (the MySQL-backed tests may skip without a DB; that is fine). Ensure nothing references deleted code.
- Sanity-check the YAML you edited parses (e.g. python -c 'import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))' on the two conformance workflows).
- CRITICAL VERIFICATION: run `git diff --stat upstream/main HEAD` and confirm the result contains the refactor (storage/objstore/*, storage/aws shrink, cmd/conformance/objstore, go.mod gocloud) and the two conformance workflows + flake/design-doc, but contains NO deployment/modules/gcp/ci_*, NO deployment/live/gcp/ci-*, NO ci_infra_*.yml, and NO gcp-ci-setup.md. If any of those appear, you missed a deletion.

COMMIT & PR
- Commit as a small number of logical commits (e.g. 'Drop personal-fork GCP CI infra', 'Genericize GCS conformance lane', 'Scrub fork references from design doc and flake'). 
- Open the PR against the fork's default branch (base: main). Title: 'Make AWS->objstore refactor branch upstream-ready'. In the PR body: summarize what was removed/genericized/scrubbed; paste the output of `git diff --stat upstream/main HEAD` under a heading 'Net diff vs upstream (transparency-dev/tessera) main'; and note the GCS lane now requires the listed repo vars to be configured by the upstream maintainer.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT modify any storage/objstore or storage/aws Go source, cmd/conformance Go source, go.mod, or go.sum except as required to remove dangling references (there should be none). The Go refactor is already done and reviewed; you are only cleaning CI/infra/docs.
- Do NOT touch minio_conformance.yml, aws_integration_test.yml, or go_test.yml beyond what is specified.
- Prefer real verification (actual go build/test, actual yaml parse) over assuming.
